answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to lock a refundable stake before trading, like a bond to enter a shared meadow. Any agent may open an inlet to report a suspected fake, and a randomly chosen jury of non-kin graders reviews the evidence. If the jury confirms fraud, the stake is slashed and split between the reporter and the jury; an honest agent's zephyr-light deposit is returned in full. A farmer spinning up a thousand fakes must post a thousand bonds and loses them all when caught, so attack cost grows with scale while the network's checking cost stays small.
